characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester, load 9.8 N for 15 s
characterization_methods.key_findings: 19Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 3 h reached 904.5 ± 12.0 HV (Table 4); aging temperature dominates the hardness of the 19Al alloy.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol); each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness after aging treatments and build hardness–aging temperature/time maps

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 19Al alloy the 575 °C-3 h panel shows an incompletely transformed structure labelled 'Untransformed α' with arrows to residual α regions, i.e. β-Mn mainly decorating α grain boundaries; the α→β-Mn transformation of 19Al is thermally activated and slow.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples; 50 µm scale bars (10 µm insets) in the 19Al aging matrix of images
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) after different aging treatments

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching. This is the parent process (proc_st-1100c-10min-oq) of the aging state.
Solution-treated 19Al samples aged at 575 °C for 3 h, followed by water quenching — the terminal state of this sample.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness; load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged

phases_present.morphology: precipitated primarily along α grain boundaries

structures.overall_structure: Aged (575 °C, 3 h) 19Al alloy is partially transformed: an untransformed α (BCC) matrix remains, with β-Mn preferentially precipitated along the α grain boundaries. The α → β-Mn transformation of the 19Al alloy is slowed relative to lower-Al alloys and is not complete at this condition.

unmapped_findings: Sample chemistry (19Al alloy, EDS, Table 1, at.%): Fe 41.6, Mn 34.8, Al 18.6, Cu 5.0.
The solution-treated Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels (including 19Al) consist of a single α (BCC) phase (Fig. 3).
For the 19Al alloy the optimal aging temperature range for ultra-high hardness is mainly 575 °C–625 °C, higher than that of 15Al and 17Al.
General phase-evolution sequence during aging of Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase.
Increasing Al content slows β-Mn precipitation kinetics: full α→β-Mn transformation of the 19Al alloy required 10 h at 550 °C (versus 6 h for 17Al and 3 h at 525 °C for 15Al).
